_comment: Verified research output for the pop-voices expansion. Authentic entries carry the source, capture timestamps and citations that were actually retrieved; nothing here is asserted from memory. Consumed by bin/seed-pop-voices.mjs.

authentic.text: I was in the middle of tweeting a very funny joke  and then a 7.1 earthquake happened and I forgot the punchline.
authentic.explanation: Posted the day after the 2019 Ridgecrest earthquake. The double space after 'joke' is his and is preserved.

authentic.text: Going out on a limb here, but doorbells and phone rings should be banned in TV commercials.
authentic.explanation: January 2020. A real grievance about a real annoyance, delivered with mock-gravitas.

authentic.text: For anyone visiting Los Angeles, I'd like to explain that addresses on North Robertson Blvd are actually to be found to the South of SOUTH Robertson Blvd
authentic.explanation: January 2019. The missing terminal punctuation is his, and the street layout really is like that.

authentic.text: This is the THIRD time I've found Jeff Goldblum in a box of Kellogg's Raisin Bran.
authentic.explanation: October 2018. The capitalised THIRD is the detail rooms argue over, and it is his.

authentic.text: The only time I regret having 3 cats is fairly often.
authentic.explanation: January 2019. A joke shape common enough that rooms assume it was written for them.

authentic.text: Would you rather be Born without a mouth or born with two mouths?
authentic.explanation: December 2018. The stray capital B on the first 'Born' is his, preserved exactly.

authentic.text: got to go to the dentist today... I need to bring my Blankie
authentic.explanation: August 2011, from his early Twitter era. Lowercase opening, trailing ellipsis, capitalised Blankie — all his.

authentic.text: If only America had Autogrill.
authentic.explanation: September 2019. Autogrill is the Italian motorway service chain — a sincere opinion that reads as a bit.

authentic.text: I am still waiting for an apple rep to come pick up my IPad. No action yey
authentic.explanation: September 2013, during her public standoff with Apple over a broken iPad. The 'yey' typo and 'IPad' capitalisation are hers.

authentic.text: I want you to go out right now and buy Fritos and cat food.
authentic.explanation: From a run of posts on the night of 2 November 2020. Delivered flat and never explained.

authentic.text: Turn off the lights and run 23 Slim Jims through the juicer.
authentic.explanation: Same night, same run. The oddly exact 23 is the detail rooms fixate on.

authentic.text: Lol. I've never eaten a Bagel in my life...
authentic.explanation: November 2018, and he meant it. The capital B on Bagel is his.

authentic.text: I am now Dionne the Singer.
authentic.explanation: December 2020, after telling Chance the Rapper to drop 'the Rapper' from his name.

authentic.text: I would say I am someone who doesn't really know what field he's in but would like to understand how the brain works.
authentic.explanation: His Nobel telephone interview, hours after winning the 2024 physics prize.

authentic.text: It is the one time in my life that I worked very, very hard!
authentic.explanation: Her Nobel telephone interview in 2018, describing the PhD work that won the prize.

authentic.text: I forgot my lines so the director wrote them down for me.
authentic.explanation: The opening line of his Best Actor speech for Raging Bull, 1981. He then read from notes.

authentic.text: It would be a lie if I told you I didn't know what to say because I've been working on this speech for about twenty-five years.
authentic.explanation: Opening his Best Actor speech for Amadeus, 1985. The twenty-five years were real.

authentic.text: Just imagine dressing the two handsomest men in the world and then getting this.
authentic.explanation: Accepting her eighth and final Oscar, for The Sting, 1974. The two men were Newman and Redford.

authentic.text: I'm playing a judge because I'm hoping to become an actual judge.
authentic.explanation: On NPR in 2010, about her recurring judge role on Law & Order. The transcript records laughter after it.

authentic.text: I've never put my own money in the show, you know. I put my talent on the line, and my money I save for Saturday night restaurants.
authentic.explanation: On Fresh Air in 2013, asked whether the advice in The Producers was his own. It was.

authentic.text: I mean, unless I'm really in my coffin, I'm going to be out there.
authentic.explanation: Roland Garros press conference, 2015, asked whether illness had made her doubt playing.

authentic.text: I didn't record it, and the chances of me watching it are less than zero.
authentic.explanation: Final Four press conference, 2022, asked if he would watch the alternate telecast.

authentic.text: No, I don't know what analytics group you work for, but no.
authentic.explanation: World Series media day, 2017, to a reporter asking about slider variation.

fabricated.text: The hotel gave me a second pillow without being asked. I've been thinking about it since Tuesday.
fabricated.explanation: Invented. Real: the mock-gravitas about small things. Invented: the pillow and the Tuesday.

fabricated.text: My dog's learned to open the pantry and has chosen to tell nobody how.
fabricated.explanation: Made up for the game. He does post about his animals; this particular betrayal is ours.

fabricated.text: is a sandwich still a sandwich if you're eating it standing up
fabricated.explanation: Not a real post. The unpunctuated would-you-rather register is his; the sandwich question is invented.

fabricated.text: the neighbours put up a new fence and nobody told me anything about it
fabricated.explanation: Invented for the game. Lowercase and unpunctuated to match his early posts; the fence is ours.

fabricated.text: The parcel says delivered. It's not delivered. I have looked everywhere including the greenhouse.
fabricated.explanation: Made up. Real: she genuinely posts customer-service grievances. Invented: the parcel and the capitalised Greenhouse.

fabricated.text: PUT THE KETTLE ON. WE ARE NOT DISCUSSING WHY.
fabricated.explanation: Written for this game. The all-caps imperative is his format; the kettle is invented.

fabricated.text: Lol. Somebody just told me a scone is not a biscuit...
fabricated.explanation: Invented. He really does post flat food revelations with a Lol opener; the scone is ours.

fabricated.text: I've never owned a plant because I refuse to be responsible for something that cannot complain.
fabricated.explanation: Not a real remark. The deadpan logic is her register; the plant is invented.

fabricated.text: You know, I bought a very expensive coat once. I still have it, and I've still not worn it outside.
fabricated.explanation: Made up for the game. The conversational run-on matches his interview voice; the coat is ours.

fabricated.text: I mean, the hotel gym had one treadmill and somebody was reading a book on it.
fabricated.explanation: Invented. The 'I mean' opener is how she actually starts press answers; the treadmill is ours.

fabricated.text: I've now been informed that the lift in this building skips the fourth floor for reasons nobody will explain
fabricated.explanation: Made up. The pedantic civic bafflement and missing full stop are his; the lift is invented.

fabricated.text: I bought a new phone and it already knows more about me than my accountant does.
fabricated.explanation: Not a real post. The single-sentence deadpan is his shape; the phone is invented.

fabricated.text: Got on the wrong train and stayed on it for a while out of politeness.
fabricated.explanation: Invented for the game. The terse travel-observation register is his; the train is ours.

fabricated.text: ok so nobody told me you can just ask for the shoes in a different size. years of this.
fabricated.explanation: Made up. The lowercase run-on enthusiasm matches her 2010-era posts; the shoes are invented.

fabricated.text: There's a spoon in this house that I like more than the others and I have started hiding it.
fabricated.explanation: Not a real post. The warm sensory domesticity is her register; the spoon is ours.

fabricated.text: I've been given a coffee with my name spelled correctly. A rare and excellent morning.
fabricated.explanation: Invented. The formal warmth is his; the coffee is ours.

fabricated.text: Lost my umbrella in a shop that only sells umbrellas. Let that one sit for a moment.
fabricated.explanation: Made up for the game. The mild wordplay shape is his; the umbrella shop is invented.

fabricated.text: ate the entire thing standing over the sink and would do it again tomorrow
fabricated.explanation: Invented. The lowercase food-guilt register is his; the sink is ours.

fabricated.text: A man in the queue told me he's had his shoes since 1998 and then walked off before I could respond.
fabricated.explanation: Not a real post. The surreal domestic anecdote is his shape; the man and his shoes are invented.

fabricated.text: Grey sky. Wind. Toast. Butter melting properly for once. Staying in.
fabricated.explanation: Made up. The fragment-stacked morning report is genuinely her format; this particular morning is ours.

fabricated.text: THIS SANDWICH HAS A SECOND SANDWICH INSIDE IT! I need everyone to know that!
fabricated.explanation: Invented for the game. The all-caps enthusiasm is his; the recursive sandwich is ours.

fabricated.text: Someone's parked so badly that I've started to admire it.
fabricated.explanation: Not a real post. The British understatement is his register; the parking is invented.

fabricated.text: I told my physio I'd felt twenty-five and he asked me to walk across the room again.
fabricated.explanation: Made up. The self-deprecating age joke matches how he actually talks in pressers; the physio is ours.
